elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's Affiliates.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly includes “Customer, its Affiliates.”

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly includes “contractors acting on Customer's behalf.”
A licence “for which Customer has paid in full” is expressly stated to be perpetual.
A licence “for which Customer has paid in full” is expressly stated to be irrevocable, and the general “revocable” qualifier was removed.

elements.element: Subscription licences may be terminated only for Customer's material breach.
elements.evidence: The clause provides that a subscription licence may be terminated by IBM “only for Customer's material breach.”

elements.element: A subscription licence may not be terminated unless the material breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: The termination trigger is expressly limited to a material breach “that remains uncured.”

elements.element: The licence is transferable to successors.
elements.evidence: Assignment without consent is permitted only to a successor organization “by merger, consolidation or acquisition.” The clause does not permit transfer to successors outside those specified M&A events.

elements.element: Customer's Affiliates are covered by the licence.
elements.evidence: Affiliates are included automatically in the licence grant, which is more protective than coverage conditioned on notice.

elements.element: Written notice is sufficient to obtain Affiliate coverage.
elements.evidence: No notice is required because Affiliates receive automatic coverage; therefore written notice cannot be a barrier to coverage.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor organization by “merger, consolidation or acquisition,” thereby transferring its contractual licence rights in those transactions.

result.reason: The redline satisfies the fallback and most preferred requirements, but it retains only an M&A-specific successor assignment right rather than general transferability to successors. It is not minimal because it also adds an unrelated backup-copy exception. That exception substantively alters the separate copying restriction, so the redline does not fully preserve unrelated commercial terms. Drafting is otherwise generally clear, although the inserted phrase “software portions of the Base Components” is awkward.
